name: Trade Submission: Executor Authorization Enforcement + Audit-Trail Integrity
description: Bootstrap-hardening of the Trade Submission tool along two pillars Andrew flagged as non-negotiable (2026-05-18): (Pillar A) the set of users permitted to execute a trade must be exactly the executors list and that must be enforced server-side -- today the trade-workflow-handler explicitly enforces NO role/group check on approve/reject/execute ('any whitelisted user can execute'), the executors group only drives notification email, and actor identity is read trustingly from the request body; (Pillar B) every trade must carry a complete, immutable, append-only record of all parties + timestamps + securities + every workflow action including failed attempts -- today state is a destructive overwrite with no event log, the EXECUTED status never durably rests (auto-advances to COMPLETE same-invocation), the execution failure path silently erases the attempt (executor_email->None), the immutable compliance JSON snapshot (json_s3_key) is never written, and rejected trades fall out of the by-approver GSI so the approver's decision history is incomplete by construction. Plus (Pillar C) the system-of-record DynamoDB table has no PITR and no deletion protection. Target architecture: canonicalize authority on the trade-users `groups` list (executors group = execute power, enforced); embedded append-only audit_events with actor+groups-snapshot+outcome and a durable EXECUTION_FAILED event; immutable submission.json compliance snapshot on execute; EXECUTED as durable terminal state; by-approver GSI repoint via a decided_at attribute; PITR + deletion protection; a managed/audited trade-users list path; and portal role-aware gating of the Execution tab. Explicitly OUT of scope per Andrew: real brokerage/custodian integration, FIX, SES production migration -- the back-office handoff (status flip + Vident Excel + email) stays as-is; this project makes it trustworthy and auditable, not different.
source_brief: Andrew direct directive 2026-05-18 during Trade Submission tool bootstrapping: 'verify that the executors list are the ones with executor power and that is enforced ... make sure that a DynamoDB row exists with all relevant data for a trade at each stage of submission/approval/execution ... tracking all parties involved and timestamps and what securities were involved. Record-keeping here is crucial, there can be no holes.' CTO investigation 2026-05-18 (workflow_handler/submission_handler/dashboard_api/excel_generator/parquet_exporter + dynamodb.tf/iam.tf + portal TradeSubmission) enumerated 5 authorization holes (A1-A5) + 8 record-keeping holes (B1-B8) in PRD section 2.
